structured_output.summary:
Ninety-nine of 100 author labels are supported by the text; one label change is recommended (holdout-175, true to false, medium confidence). The holdout is well constructed: each positive isolates one empty sentence between concrete neighbors, and the neighbors consistently fail to resolve the specific defect, so the "causal word or number is not blanket protection" rule holds throughout. Negatives consistently supply the cause, definition, or sequence that the apparent target construction promises.

The one recurring boundary problem is attribution. The rulebook protects "attributed evaluations and quotations discussed as someone else's wording," but the author labels only preserve reported wording when the paragraph explicitly critiques it and then supplies the missing content (131, 157, 186, 195, 197). Reported speech alone ("staff said", "reviewers said", "the treasurer described", "the plan promised", "the curator described") is treated as non-protective in 116, 119, 123, 138, 142, 145, 156, 169, 194. That practice is internally consistent and defensible for vague-change and metaphor targets, where the rulebook grants no attribution exemption, but it sits uneasily with the Unsupported Significance no-hit "The 2025 audit called the platform a visionary approach to education." Records 145 and 156 are the closest to that exemption and are marked medium confidence. Holdout-175 is the case where the author's practice and the rulebook text diverge: the paragraph reports the letter's toll metaphor and explicitly judges it indefinite, so its own claim is concrete even though it never replaces the figure; the author reason also misdescribes the paragraph as announcing the expense itself. Holdout-138 lacks any explicit critique clause, so its true label stands at medium confidence; the pair 138/175 should be used to decide whether critique-without-replacement protects.

No author reason contains a factual misdescription of paragraph contents apart from the stance issue in 175. Minor note: 183 contains an uncited gaze beat (score sheet, then floor); it is not needed for the label.
